title: The covalent model
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for IB Diploma Chemistry (status of the source: ai-reviewed-reverified-gate-verified-2026-09-30-awaiting-human-signoff). Terms and clues: S2.2#c28 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; S2.2#c29 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; S2.2#c22 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; S2.2#c20 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition. Questions: S2.2#q11, S2.2#q14, S2.2#q17, S2.2#q20, S2.2#q12, S2.2#q15, S2.2#q18, S2.2#q21, S2.2#q13, S2.2#q16, S2.2#q19, S2.2#q34, S2.2#q22, S2.2#q24, S2.2#q26, S2.2#q28, S2.2#q30, S2.2#q32.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Dipole–dipole forces
items.clue: Attractions between the permanent partial charges of neighbouring polar molecules.

items.label: Hydrogen bond
items.clue: An attraction between H joined to N, O or F and a lone pair on a nearby N, O or F.

items.label: Fullerene (C₆₀)
items.clue: A molecular allotrope of carbon: a closed, ball-shaped cage of pentagons and hexagons.

items.label: Graphite
items.clue: Each carbon atom is covalently bonded to three others in flat layers of hexagonal rings.

questions.stem: Graphite conducts electricity. Which feature of its structure explains this?

options.text: It contains carbon ions that move through the layers when a voltage is applied
Its atoms are held by metallic bonding, as its shiny grey appearance suggests
Each carbon atom bonds to three others, leaving one electron per atom delocalized
Its layers slide over one another easily, carrying electric charge as they move

questions.explanation: In each layer every carbon atom forms three covalent bonds. Its fourth valence electron is delocalized across the layer, and these mobile electrons carry the current along the layers.

questions.stem: Hydrogen chloride gas is mixed with iodine vapour. Which intermolecular forces act between an HCl molecule and an I₂ molecule?

options.text: London forces only, as I₂ is a non-polar molecule with no dipole
London and dipole–induced dipole forces, as HCl polarizes the I₂ molecule
London and dipole–dipole forces, as the HCl molecules are polar
London forces and hydrogen bonds, as HCl has H bonded to electronegative Cl

questions.explanation: London forces act between all molecules. HCl also has a permanent dipole, which induces a temporary dipole in the non-polar I₂ molecule, giving a dipole–induced dipole attraction.

questions.stem: Propane, CH₃CH₂CH₃ (M_r 44.11), ethanal, CH₃CHO (M_r 44.06), and ethanol, CH₃CH₂OH (M_r 46.08), have comparable molar masses. Which lists them in order of increasing boiling point?

options.text: propane < ethanal < ethanol
propane < ethanol < ethanal
ethanal < propane < ethanol
ethanal < ethanol < propane

questions.explanation: With comparable molar masses the type of intermolecular force decides. Propane has only London forces (−42 °C); ethanal is polar and adds dipole–dipole forces (20 °C); ethanol forms hydrogen bonds (78 °C).

questions.stem: In a paper chromatography experiment the baseline was drawn 1.0 cm above the bottom edge of the paper. At the end, the solvent front was 11.0 cm above the bottom edge and the centre of a spot was 4.4 cm above the bottom edge. What is the RF value of the spot?
questions.explanation: Distance moved by the spot = 4.4 − 1.0 = 3.4 cm; distance moved by the solvent = 11.0 − 1.0 = 10.0 cm. RF = 3.4 ÷ 10.0 = 0.34.

questions.stem: Which statement about carbon allotropes or silicon is correct?

options.text: Diamond has a very high melting point because of strong intermolecular forces
C₆₀ fullerene is a giant covalent network, so like diamond it has a very high melting point
Silicon conducts electricity because its atoms are held together by metallic bonding
Graphene conducts electricity as each atom bonds to three others, leaving delocalized electrons

questions.explanation: Graphene is a single layer of graphite: each carbon atom forms three covalent bonds in hexagonal rings, and its fourth valence electron is delocalized across the layer, so the layer conducts electricity.

questions.stem: Liquid methanol, CH₃OH, contains hydrogen bonds. What is a hydrogen bond in methanol?

options.text: An attraction between the H of an O–H group and a lone pair on O in another molecule
The covalent bond between the O atom and the H atom within one methanol molecule
An attraction between the H atoms of one molecule and the H atoms of another
An attraction between an H atom of the CH₃ group and an O atom in a neighbouring molecule

questions.explanation: A hydrogen bond forms when hydrogen, covalently bonded to an electronegative atom (here O), is attracted to a lone pair on an electronegative atom (O) of a neighbouring molecule.

questions.stem: Which of the following conducts electricity?

options.text: Liquid sulfur
Diamond crystal
Solid graphite
Ethanol in water

questions.explanation: In graphite each carbon atom is covalently bonded to three others, and its fourth valence electron is delocalized across the layer. These mobile electrons carry a current.

questions.stem: A mixture is separated by paper chromatography. Under the same conditions, component X has an RF value of 0.20 and component Y has an RF value of 0.75. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Relative to the mobile phase, X is attracted more strongly to the stationary phase than Y is
X has larger molecules than Y, so the fibres of the paper hold X back more than Y
X would also reach an RF of 0.75 if the solvent were allowed to run for a longer time
X is less soluble in the solvent than Y, and the paper plays no part in the separation

questions.stem: Carbon dioxide sublimes at −78 °C, but silicon dioxide melts at about 1700 °C. Which statement explains the difference?

options.text: Subliming CO₂ breaks its C=O bonds, which are weaker than the Si–O bonds in SiO₂
SiO₂ molecules are heavier than CO₂ molecules, so their London forces are stronger
SiO₂ is a giant covalent network, but CO₂ is made of small separate molecules
SiO₂ is an ionic solid of Si⁴⁺ and O²⁻ ions, like other oxides with high melting points

questions.explanation: In SiO₂ each Si atom is covalently bonded to four O atoms and each O atom to two Si atoms, so melting breaks many strong covalent bonds. CO₂ is made of separate molecules, and subliming it overcomes only weak London forces between them.

questions.stem: Which statement about the intermolecular forces between molecules of propanone, CH₃COCH₃, is correct?

options.text: They include hydrogen bonds, as each propanone molecule contains H and O atoms
They include no London forces, as propanone molecules are polar
They include London forces, which are the only kind of van der Waals force
They include dipole–dipole forces, which count as van der Waals forces

questions.explanation: Propanone is polar: the C=O bond is polar and the bond dipoles do not cancel. So dipole–dipole forces act between its molecules, alongside London forces, and both are included in the term van der Waals forces.

questions.stem: Ethanol, CH₃CH₂OH, mixes with water in all proportions, but hexane, C₆H₁₄, does not dissolve in water. Which statement explains this difference?

options.text: Ethanol splits into ions that water surrounds, but hexane does not form ions
Ethanol can form hydrogen bonds with water molecules, but hexane cannot
Hexane is less dense than water, so it floats on the water rather than dissolving
Hexane molecules are too large to fit into the gaps between water molecules

questions.explanation: The O–H group of ethanol forms hydrogen bonds with water, replacing the hydrogen bonds broken between water molecules. Hexane forms only London forces with water, far weaker than the hydrogen bonds it would have to break, so it does not dissolve.

questions.stem: Silicon is a shiny grey solid that melts at 1414 °C, conducts electricity only slightly and does not dissolve in water or in hexane. Which describes the structure of solid silicon?

options.text: A lattice of positive Si ions in a sea of delocalized electrons, as in metals
A network in which each Si atom is covalently bonded to four others, as in diamond
Separate silicon molecules held together by strong intermolecular forces
Flat layers in which each Si atom is bonded to three others, as in graphite

questions.explanation: Each Si atom forms four covalent bonds to other Si atoms in a tetrahedral three-dimensional network, as C does in diamond. Melting breaks many strong Si–Si bonds, hence 1414 °C, and no solvent can separate the atoms.

questions.stem: Ozone, O₃, can be represented by two Lewis formulas that differ only in which O–O bond is shown as the double bond. Which describes the bonds in a real ozone molecule?

options.text: One single and one double bond, fixed in place exactly as one of the two Lewis formulas shows
Two identical bonds, intermediate between single and double, as electrons are delocalized
Two double bonds, with the central oxygen atom expanding its octet to ten electrons
One single and one double bond, which swap positions rapidly back and forth

questions.stem: The enthalpy change of hydrogenation of cyclohexene (one C=C bond) is about −120 kJ mol⁻¹. For benzene, forming cyclohexane, it is about −208 kJ mol⁻¹, much less exothermic than the −360 kJ mol⁻¹ predicted for a structure with three localized C=C bonds. Which statement explains the difference?

options.text: Breaking benzene's delocalized bonds releases less energy than breaking three C=C bonds
Benzene has only one or two C=C bonds, since 208 lies between 1 × 120 and 2 × 120
Benzene reacts incompletely with hydrogen, so less energy is released per mole
Delocalization lowers benzene's energy, so less energy is released as it is hydrogenated

questions.stem: In sulfur tetrafluoride, SF₄, the sulfur atom (six valence electrons) forms a single bond to each of four fluorine atoms. What is the molecular geometry of SF₄?

options.text: Tetrahedral, as only the four bonding pairs repel one another around sulfur
Trigonal bipyramidal, as there are five electron domains around the sulfur atom
Trigonal pyramidal, as the lone pair takes an axial site in a trigonal bipyramid
See-saw, as the lone pair takes an equatorial site in a trigonal bipyramid

questions.explanation: Sulfur uses four of its six valence electrons in bonds and keeps one lone pair: five electron domains, trigonal bipyramidal. The lone pair takes an equatorial position (fewer 90° repulsions), leaving the four F atoms in a see-saw shape.

questions.stem: In the Lewis formula of carbon monoxide, C and O are joined by a triple bond and each atom has one lone pair. Using FC = V − N − ½B (V = valence electrons of the free atom, N = non-bonding electrons, B = bonding electrons), what is the formal charge on the carbon atom?
questions.explanation: V = 4, N = 2 (one lone pair), B = 6 (three shared pairs). FC = 4 − 2 − ½ × 6 = −1.

questions.stem: How many σ (sigma) bonds are there in one molecule of propenenitrile, CH₂=CH–C≡N?
questions.explanation: Three C–H bonds (3 σ), the C=C bond (1 σ + 1 π), the C–C bond (1 σ) and the C≡N bond (1 σ + 2 π): 3 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 6 σ bonds (and 3 π bonds).

questions.stem: In ethanenitrile, CH₃CN, the nitrogen atom is joined to carbon by a triple bond and carries one lone pair. What is the hybridization of the nitrogen atom?

options.text: sp, as it has two electron domains: the triple bond and the lone pair
sp², as it forms three bonds to the carbon atom, one for each shared pair
sp³, as nitrogen is sp³ hybridized in ammonia and keeps that in its compounds
Not hybridized, as only carbon atoms form hybrid orbitals in molecules

questions.explanation: The triple bond counts as one electron domain and the lone pair as another. Two domains correspond to sp hybridization, with the domains at 180°; the two unhybridized p orbitals form the two π bonds.
